summary.description: DeepCAC2 is a two-stage deep learning pipeline for coronary artery calcification assessment in chest CT. It first uses an nnU-Net-based cardiac segmentation model to localize the heart, then applies a patch-based 3D U-Net to segment coronary artery calcifications and derive coronary artery calcium scores (CACS) and risk categories.

inputs.label: Chest CT
inputs.description: Non-contrast, low-dose chest CT scan in DICOM format.

outputs.label: Predicted CAC Score
outputs.description: Automated coronary artery calcium score derived from the predicted CAC segmentation.

outputs.label: Calcium measurements
outputs.description: Calcium volume, CAC segmentation volume, lesion count, and individual lesion measurements.

model.architecture: Two-stage pipeline with nnU-Net-based cardiac segmentation followed by patch-based 3D U-Net CAC segmentation.

publications.title: Coronary artery calcification assessment in National Lung Screening Trial CT images (DeepCAC2)

use.title: Intended use
use.text: DeepCAC2 supports research on automated coronary artery calcification (CAC) segmentation, calcium scoring, and opportunistic cardiovascular risk assessment from non-contrast chest CT. The model was used to process the National Lung Screening Trial (NLST) chest CT collection. The resulting dataset of CAC segmentations, calcium scores, and lesion measurements is distributed through Zenodo. An interactive public dashboard enables cohort exploration and case-level inspection of the results [1], with source CT images accessible through the Imaging Data Commons (IDC) [2]. The model has not been validated for clinical decision-making.

analyses.title: Analyses
analyses.text: The pipeline produces volumetric segmentations of the heart and coronary artery calcifications. Coronary artery calcium scores (CACS) are calculated using the Agatston method and assigned to the risk groups listed below. Outputs also include calcium volume, CAC segmentation volume, lesion count, and individual lesion measurements. These outputs support cohort stratification, longitudinal analyses, survival modeling, and imaging biomarker research [1].

evaluation.title: Evaluation
evaluation.text: Technical validation compared model-derived CACS and score categories with expert-derived values for 380 NLST CT series. An adjusted Cox analysis assessed associations between model-derived CAC categories and all-cause mortality in 22,741 participants [1].

entries.Adjusted covariates: Age, sex, smoking status, heart disease

training.title: Training
training.text: The CAC segmentation model was developed using 777 ECG-gated cardiac CT series from the Framingham Heart Study with expert CAC annotations: 622 for training and 155 for internal validation. The pipeline first localizes the heart using a separate nnU-Net-based cardiac segmentation model, then applies the CAC model trained on balanced overlapping 3D patches extracted from heart-centered volumes [1].

limitations.title: Limitations
limitations.text: The model is optimized for non-contrast, low-dose chest CT scans and may be sensitive to variations in acquisition protocols, reconstruction parameters, and image quality. CAC quantification is derived from non-ECG-gated scans, which may introduce motion-related inaccuracies compared to dedicated cardiac CT. Generalization to other populations, scanners, and clinical workflows requires further validation [1].
